verdict.rationale: Aider auto-commits every AI edit to git with descriptive messages and '(aider)' author attribution. Users can review those changes in git history, roll them back with /undo, and manage history with /git, so scripted runs (--message, the Python Coder API) produce versioned, reviewable, reversible outputs. However, this versioning applies to the code changes the automation makes, not to the automations themselves; scripts and .aider.conf.yml can only be versioned as ordinary files in the user's repo. Missing for 10: first-class versioning, review and rollback of automation definitions (scripts/config) themselves, and independent corroboration of the rollback workflow in scripted/automated use.
